maintenance.reason: Alpha9.57 fixes the first-refresh startup regression exposed immediately after installing Alpha9.56: the canonical commissioning compatibility wrappers now accept and forward the provisional data_override payload used by the coordinator before coordinator.data exists, and tariff reconciliation reads that same provisional snapshot. The Alpha9.47 diagnostics compatibility layer is also pass-through for the new keyword and no longer overwrites the current bounded-control commissioning wording with the obsolete pre-control hard-block message. This is a startup/compatibility hotfix only; it does not broaden FoxESS write authority, does not enable Agile or paid export control, does not make Force Discharge or Export Power Limit writes live, and leaves the 10 W grid-import-prevention bias Shadow-only. Alpha9.56 introduces the first bounded opt-in real FoxESS control backend for non-Agile operation. Live writes are limited to Self Use, confirmed-cheap-period Force Charge and Min SoC-on-grid on the uniquely bound authoritative FoxESS device, and only when Control mode, Master control enable, the separate Commissioned for control acknowledgement, full control-critical commissioning readiness, a fresh safe plan, the complete KEMS preflight suite, on-grid operation, no emergency stop, No paid export mode and the exact reviewed foxess_modbus v1.15.0 contract all pass together. Before taking ownership KEMS persists the pre-control local FoxESS work mode and Min SoC-on-grid, and losing any authority gate releases KEMS ownership and restores those values. Deliberate Force Discharge, paid or Agile economic export control, the Alpha9.55 Grid import prevention bias and FoxESS Export Power Limit writes remain outside the live-control scope; the 10 W bias remains Shadow-only because the reviewed FoxESS remote active-power command is an inverter active-power setpoint rather than a proven net-grid-power target. Overall reporting data quality is informational for control commissioning and cannot by itself unlock writes; the control-critical FoxESS unit, telemetry-stability, battery-direction, grid-direction, whole-site power-balance, tariff, planner, limit, emergency-stop and unique command-surface evidence remains fail-closed. Alpha9.56 does not broaden Ohme authority and does not enable Agile tariff export control. Alpha9.55 adds an optional user-selected Grid import prevention bias from 0 to 100 W, with a safe default of 0 W disabled. When KEMS would otherwise sit near zero grid exchange, the Shadow control path may model a tiny export trim such as 10 W to avoid a few watts of standing grid import. This bias is operational trim rather than paid or economic export: No paid export still values export income at zero and normal economic battery-export authority remains disabled. The bias is suppressed in Observe, emergency stop, stale or unsafe plans, island/EPS operation, cheap charging, deliberate economic export, at or below the active SOC reserve, outside the +/-100 W grid trim window, or when KEMS export, inverter or discharge headroom is insufficient. Command Shadow exposes the configured bias, target and observed grid power, active or suppressed state and suppression reason, and represents an active bias as a tiny Force Discharge/export-limit proposal while commands_permitted remains false and real FoxESS hardware writes remain blocked. Alpha9.55 does not enable Control, commissioning completion, a real backend or any FoxESS hardware write. Alpha9.54 separates the user-selected KEMS export ceiling from the FoxESS installer/current hardware export ceiling. The dedicated read-only FoxESS export-limit sensor is now treated as independent hardware-maximum evidence rather than a value that must equal the KEMS setting: a KEMS ceiling at or below the observed FoxESS hardware ceiling passes commissioning compatibility, a KEMS ceiling above the observed hardware ceiling fails closed, and a missing, ambiguous or unusable authoritative readback waits rather than guessing. The effective physical export ceiling is the lower of the KEMS user ceiling and the observed FoxESS hardware ceiling. Command Shadow independently applies that lower effective ceiling to both the proposed FoxESS export-power limit and deliberate Force Discharge power. A user-selected KEMS ceiling of 0 kW is valid and means never deliberately export. The proven live case FoxESS 14.5 kW / KEMS 6.4 kW therefore resolves to an effective 6.4 kW ceiling without changing the installer setting. No-paid-export operation still proposes a transient 0 W export limit and no Force Discharge, while Full-KEMS counterfactual simulation remains separate. Alpha9.54 does not enable Control, commissioning completion, a real backend or any FoxESS hardware write; ready_for_control remains false, commands remain blocked and Simulate remains read-only. Alpha9.53 introduced the dedicated read-only FoxESS export-limit commissioning proof and remains retained as the readback/binding foundation for this revised authority model. Alpha9.52 fixes the Shadow/physical control authority boundary exposed by live Alpha9.51 diagnostics. The Full-KEMS rolling optimiser remains authoritative for counterfactual simulation and may continue to model profitable battery export, but the physical ControlState now projects that target through live export permission and island state before it can become FoxESS command intent. No-paid-export or island operation clamps deliberate physical battery export to 0 kW while preserving house-support discharge, and the FoxESS command shadow independently fails closed if deliberate export is ever presented while grid export is disabled. The configured 6.4 kW physical/DNO export capability remains reported separately from the active 0 W no-export command allowance. Alpha9.52 does not enable Control, commissioning, a real backend, or any FoxESS hardware write; all existing command and commissioning gates remain closed and Simulate remains read-only. Alpha9.51 retains a bounded deduplicated history of completed Power Down sessions, exposes every completed session for the current local day on the managed KEMS dashboard, restores an explicit Power Down event-credit row to KEMS Daily costs, and makes retained completed-event bonus evidence authoritative for completed same-day customer reporting instead of continuing to show a stale in-event estimate. Completed-event figures remain KEMS retained results rather than supplier-settled Octopus cash. Alpha9.51 is reporting, persistence and presentation only: no Power Down joining, optimiser or dispatch decisions, tariff or SOC policy, commissioning, control eligibility, Ohme authority or FoxESS hardware-write authority changes; real hardware writes remain hard-blocked. Retained successor contracts include the Alpha9 coordinated parity baseline; Alpha9.13 forecast-aware scheduling; Alpha9.19 runtime Recorder hygiene; Alpha9.20 ShadowValidationRecorder Recorder hygiene; the Alpha9.22 startup hotfix at build_slot_flow for the unexpected planning_target_soc_percent keyword; the Alpha9.24 flow parity export-floor correction with its 15% planning/export target, independent 10% absolute floor and restart-safe 12% recovery latch; Alpha9.25 observability and reporting-only 7.0 kW cheap-window charge capability; Alpha9.27 reporting-only policy-label publication; Alpha9.28 staggered V2 flow while V1 remains unchanged and no optimiser behaviour changes; Alpha9.29 extra gap V2 packet spacing while V1 remains unchanged and no optimiser behaviour changes; Alpha9.30 solar-only commissioning; Alpha9.37 canonical current-day KEMS cost dashboard parity as presentation/reporting only with no FoxESS command/write authority changes; Alpha9.44 dashboard/observability only for Weekend Happy Hour with no Happy Hour scoring or joining logic changes and no FoxESS hardware-write authority change; Alpha9.45 reward normalisation where raw 6 reports 3 rewards rather than 6, the two-one-hour-reward event-day limit and 16 kWh-per-reward-hour cap, and it does not broaden external Octopus booking authority or FoxESS hardware-write authority; Alpha9.46 Solar Generation Today authority with telemetry gaps retained as discrepancy evidence; Alpha9.48 physical daily authority for Load Energy Today, Grid Consumption Today and Feed-in Today; Alpha9.49 Power Down dashboard/observability with joining unchanged and FoxESS hardware-write authority unchanged; and Alpha9.50 final managed dashboard composition preserving Weekend Happy Hour and Power Down presentation. All prior Alpha9 safety, reporting and control contracts remain retained.
